To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the software development processes in ISO 262062 Part 6 can be applied to ML, with some adaptations and extensions; (ii) the adaptations and extensions are not significant, and are mostly related to documentation and traceability; (iii) the software processes in ISO 26 262 can be applied to supervised learning, but not to other types of ML; (iv) the software processes can be applied to the development of an ADAS, but not to the development of ADS
• The key conflict in the use of ML in ISO 262262 is that ML is not a traditional software development technology.

• The ISO 26262 software process requirements in Part 6 are not sufficient for ML, and • The proposed adaptation and extension to ISO 26262 Part 6 is sufficient to address the gaps in ISO 2626 for ML.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of machine learning (and in particular supervised learning) to automotive systems.
the question of how to adapt and extend ISO 26262 in order to accommodate ML.
the use of machine learning in automotive software development, and specifically in ADAS and ADS development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ML is not a panacea for safety, but it can be used to improve safety in the right context, with appropriate design and engineering practices, and with appropriate safety assurance methods.
the use of ML in automotive systems is not a problem in itself, but rather the lack of appropriate safety requirements for ML.
the use of ML is not a threat to safety in an automotive environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current version of ISO 262624 is not sufficient for ML.

• We identified the main sources of conflict between ML and safety standards, • We assessed each requirement of ISO 26264 Part 6 to determine if and how it applies to ML development scenarios, • We identified gaps where new requirements are needed, • We provided a detailed proposal for new requirements that address these gaps, and • We discussed how the new requirements could be applied to ML development scenarios.

we have: (1) identified key factors that contribute to the conflict between the need for innovation and safety in the context of ML, (2) performed a detailed assessment of each requirement from ISO 26262:2018 Part 6 for its applicability to ML, and (3) proposed new requirements to address identified gaps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the requirements of ISO 262624 can be adapted to accommodate supervised ML in automotive development.
ML is not a panacea for safety, and that there is a need to be cautious and thoughtful when applying ML to safety critical systems.
ML can be developed safely in an ISO 26262 context, but the current version of ISO 262262 is not adequate to do so.
